As we mark Banned Books Week, it is a vital time to look back at how we got here. Launched in 1982 by legendary library activist Judith Krug, this week was founded during a massive surge in book challenges across schools and libraries in the United States. It serves as a reminder that the suppression of ideas isn't new, but neither is our collective duty to stand against it. 

Here in Western New York, our libraries are some of our most important community spaces. They’re where kids fall in love with reading, where families find resources, and where everyone can learn something new, for free. 

Stop by your local library this week and pick up a book. Drop your favorite in the comments below 👇
